# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## A Plan for Every Stage of Life

The Conservative Party presents a comprehensive vision for Britain built on the success of their long-term economic plan, which they credit with transforming Britain from economic crisis to the fastest-growing major advanced economy. The manifesto emphasizes that this recovery, achieved through difficult decisions and national sacrifice, remains fragile and could be reversed by wrong choices—implicitly contrasting their economic competence with Labour's record.

## Economic Foundation

The Conservatives pledge to eliminate the deficit through balanced, sensible measures: continuing spending reductions of one per cent annually, finding £12 billion in welfare savings, and raising £5 billion from tackling tax evasion. They commit to running a surplus by 2018-19, arguing this is both economically necessary and morally right—refusing to burden future generations with debt. Crucially, they promise no increases in VAT, Income Tax, or National Insurance, instead raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000.

## Rewarding Hard Work

Central to the Conservative vision is ensuring work always pays. They will create three million apprenticeships, introduce a Tax-Free Minimum Wage, and continue welfare reforms including reducing the benefit cap to £23,000. Universal Credit will ensure people are always better off working. Young people aged 18-21 will face tougher requirements, with Jobseeker's Allowance replaced by a time-limited Youth Allowance requiring community contribution.

## Supporting Families

The Conservatives will extend the Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants, build 200,000 Starter Homes at 20 per cent below market price for first-time buyers under 40, and provide 30 hours free childcare for working parents. They support marriage through transferable tax allowances and will take the family home out of Inheritance Tax by raising the effective threshold to £1 million for couples.

## Public Services

The NHS will receive at least £8 billion additional funding by 2020, delivering truly seven-day services and same-day GP appointments for over-75s. Education reforms will continue, with every failing school becoming an academy, 500 new free schools, and protected per-pupil funding. The Conservatives emphasize backing great teachers, rigorous standards, and parental choice.

## Immigration and EU Reform

Recognizing public concern about uncontrolled immigration, the Conservatives will reform welfare rules to require EU migrants to work here for four years before claiming benefits. They commit to an in-out EU referendum by end of 2017, seeking renegotiation to return powers from Brussels while maintaining Single Market access. They will scrap the Human Rights Act, introducing a British Bill of Rights.

## Security and Values

The manifesto promises maintained defence spending, Trident renewal, and strengthened counter-terrorism powers. They will confront all forms of extremism, including non-violent extremism, while championing British values. The Armed Forces Covenant will be honoured, and the 0.7 per cent international development commitment maintained.

## Devolution and Union

English votes for English laws will address the West Lothian Question, while honouring commitments to Scottish devolution and Welsh powers. The Conservatives present themselves as the party of the Union, having secured the Scottish independence referendum result.

## Conclusion

The Conservatives present a clear choice: their proven economic competence versus the risk of Labour's higher taxes, more borrowing, and economic chaos. They ask voters to trust the team that delivered recovery to complete the job, building a Britain where aspiration is rewarded, families are supported, and everyone can achieve their potential.
